purpose: Bidirectional archaic<->modern surface model for the OriginalDR reconstruction (plan §6.1). It documents the type-level glyph correspondences and the lexical period-spelling patterns that separate the 1582/1609-1610 Rheims-Douay archaic orthography (idx 109) from the modern rendering (idx 108). Its operational use is the FOLD: both renderings are reduced to a spelling/glyph-neutral skeleton so the §6.2 word-for-word correspondence check isolates genuine wording differences from expected orthographic variation. The rules are the same ones the archaic witnesses exhibit and the modern edition normalizes away.

glyph_rules.name: long-s
glyph_rules.note: U+017F LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S. NFKD-decomposes to 's', so the fold neutralizes it type-agnostically. Diplomatic rendering keeps ſ from the archaic witness; it is NOT introduced by transform.

glyph_rules.name: double-v
glyph_rules.note: archaic compositors set w as double-v

glyph_rules.name: u-v-positional
glyph_rules.note: archaic uses v initially and u medially/finally regardless of sound (vpon/upon, haue/have, vnto/unto). Not a 1:1 map, so the fold collapses u and v to a single class for comparison; diplomatic rendering restores the positional form from the archaic witness.

glyph_rules.name: i-j-positional
glyph_rules.archaic: i for both i and j
glyph_rules.note: archaic uses i for i and j (iustice/justice, Iesvs/Jesus). The fold collapses i and j; diplomatic rendering restores the archaic form from the witness.

period_spelling_patterns.note: archaic -aie-/-ie-/-y- variation; the fold maps y->i and is not a clean inverse

fold.name: fold_diplomatic
fold.description: Per-word archaic-and-modern -> neutral lower-case skeleton. Applied to both idx 108 and idx 109 surfaces before token comparison. Order matters.
steps: NFKD normalise + drop combining marks (folds ſ->s and diacritics such as õ->o)
æ->ae, œ->oe (NFKD leaves these base letters intact)
v->u and j->i (collapse the positional u/v and i/j classes)
collapse any run of a repeated letter to one (doubled consonants/vowels)
fold.excludes: The OCR-tolerance SYMMETRIC f<->s of ocr_sample.skel is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. That rule was built to tolerate tesseract misreading long-ſ as 'f'; folding it here would MASK the fresh-OCR long-ſ->f defect as a match and hide a real diplomatic-fidelity problem in the OCR-only books (Isaie, Ecclesiasticus, the prophets). §6.2 must SEE that defect, so the fold keeps f and s distinct.

worked_examples.note: long-ſ folds to s via NFKD; 'blessed' collapses doubled ss -> 'blesed'; 'the' loses its silent -e -> 'th'. Modern and archaic surfaces fold identically.

worked_examples.modern: In the beginning God created heaven and earth
worked_examples.archaic: In the beginning God created heauen and earth
worked_examples.note: 'beginning' collapses nn -> 'begining'; modern 'heaven' and archaic 'heauen' both fold to 'heauen' (v->u collapse).
positional u/v and i/j classes collapse: have/haue->hau, upon/vpon->upon, justice/iustice->iustic, Jesus/Iesvs->iesus. Every modern/archaic pair folds to one skeleton.

non_reversible_note: The positional u/v & i/j classes and the period-spelling patterns are LOSSY: the fold neutralises them for COMPARISON only. Archaic RENDERING (idx 109) restores every archaic surface form from the archaic witness itself (s-dismas / odr-com / OCR), never from a back-transform of the modern text — so no lossy inverse is applied to produce the gold text (plan §5.3, §6.1).
